source: fdmprinter.def.json (base definition for all CuraEngine printers)
note: These are the settings available in [slicer.cura.overrides]. Use the 'key' field as the override key.

settings.label: Build volume fan number
settings.description: The number of the fan that cools the build volume. If this is set to 0, it's means that there is no build volume fan

settings.label: Machine Type
settings.description: The name of your 3D printer model.

settings.label: Show Machine Variants
settings.description: Whether to show the different variants of this machine, which are described in separate json files.

settings.label: Start G-code
settings.description: G-code commands to be executed at the very start - separated by \n.
settings.default:
G28 ;Home
G1 Z15.0 F6000 ;Move the platform down 15mm
;Prime the extruder
G92 E0
G1 F200 E3
G92 E0

settings.label: End G-code
settings.description: G-code commands to be executed at the very end - separated by \n.
settings.default:
M104 S0
M140 S0
;Retract the filament
G92 E1
G1 E-1 F300
G28 X0 Y0
M84

settings.label: Material GUID
settings.description: GUID of the material. This is set automatically.

settings.label: Material Type
settings.description: The type of material used.

settings.label: Material Brand
settings.description: The brand of material used.

settings.label: Diameter
settings.description: Adjusts the diameter of the filament used. Match this value with the diameter of the used filament.

settings.label: Wait for Build Plate Heatup
settings.description: Whether to insert a command to wait until the build plate temperature is reached at the start.

settings.label: Wait for Nozzle Heatup
settings.description: Whether to wait until the nozzle temperature is reached at the start.

settings.label: Include Material Temperatures
settings.description: Whether to include nozzle temperature commands at the start of the gcode. When the start_gcode already contains nozzle temperature commands Cura frontend will automatically disable this setting.

settings.label: Include Build Plate Temperature
settings.description: Whether to include build plate temperature commands at the start of the gcode. When the start_gcode already contains build plate temperature commands Cura frontend will automatically disable this setting.

settings.label: Machine Width
settings.description: The width (X-direction) of the printable area.

settings.label: Machine Depth
settings.description: The depth (Y-direction) of the printable area.

settings.label: Machine Height
settings.description: The height (Z-direction) of the printable area.

settings.label: Build Plate Shape
settings.description: The shape of the build plate without taking unprintable areas into account.

settings.label: Build Plate Type
settings.description: The type of build plate installed on the printer.

settings.label: Has Heated Build Plate
settings.description: Whether the machine has a heated build plate present.

settings.label: Has Build Volume Temperature Stabilization
settings.description: Whether the machine is able to stabilize the build volume temperature.

settings.label: Always Write Active Tool
settings.description: Write active tool after sending temp commands to inactive tool. Required for Dual Extruder printing with Smoothie or other firmware with modal tool commands.

settings.label: Is Center Origin
settings.description: Whether the X/Y coordinates of the zero position of the printer is at the center of the printable area.

settings.label: Number of Extruders
settings.description: Number of extruder trains. An extruder train is the combination of a feeder, bowden tube, and nozzle.

settings.label: Number of Extruders That Are Enabled
settings.description: Number of extruder trains that are enabled; automatically set in software

settings.label: Outer Nozzle Diameter
settings.description: The outer diameter of the tip of the nozzle.

settings.label: Nozzle Angle
settings.description: The angle between the horizontal plane and the conical part right above the tip of the nozzle.

settings.label: Heat Zone Length
settings.description: The distance from the tip of the nozzle in which heat from the nozzle is transferred to the filament.

settings.label: Enable Nozzle Temperature Control
settings.description: Whether to control temperature from Cura. Turn this off to control nozzle temperature from outside of Cura.

settings.label: Heat Up Speed
settings.description: The speed (°C/s) by which the nozzle heats up averaged over the window of normal printing temperatures and the standby temperature.

settings.label: Cool Down Speed
settings.description: The speed (°C/s) by which the nozzle cools down averaged over the window of normal printing temperatures and the standby temperature.

settings.label: Minimal Time Standby Temperature
settings.description: The minimal time an extruder has to be inactive before the nozzle is cooled. Only when an extruder is not used for longer than this time will it be allowed to cool down to the standby temperature.

settings.label: G-code Flavor
settings.description: The type of g-code to be generated.

settings.label: Firmware Retraction
settings.description: Whether to use firmware retract commands (G10/G11) instead of using the E property in G1 commands to retract the material.

settings.label: Extruders Share Heater
settings.description: Whether the extruders share a single heater rather than each extruder having its own heater.

settings.label: Extruders Share Nozzle
settings.description: Whether the extruders share a single nozzle rather than each extruder having its own nozzle. When set to true, it is expected that the printer-start gcode script properly sets up all extruders in an initial retraction state that is known and mutually compatible (either zero or one filament not retracted); in that case the initial retraction status is described, per extruder, by the 'machine_extruders_shared_nozzle_initial_retraction' parameter.

settings.label: Shared Nozzle Initial Retraction
settings.description: How much the filament of each extruder is assumed to have been retracted from the shared nozzle tip at the completion of the printer-start gcode script; the value should be equal to or greater than the length of the common part of the nozzle's ducts.

settings.label: Disallowed Areas
settings.description: A list of polygons with areas the print head is not allowed to enter.

settings.label: Nozzle Disallowed Areas
settings.description: A list of polygons with areas the nozzle is not allowed to enter.

settings.label: Machine Head & Fan Polygon
settings.description: The dimensions of the print head used to determine 'Safe Model Distance' when printing 'One at a Time'. These numbers relate to the centerline of the first extruder nozzle. Left of the nozzle is 'X Min' and must be negative.  Rear of the nozzle is 'Y Min' and must be negative.  X Max (right) and Y Max (front) are positive numbers.  Gantry height is the dimension from the build plate to the X gantry beam.

settings.label: Gantry Height
settings.description: The height difference between the tip of the nozzle and the gantry system (X and Y axes).

settings.label: Print Time Estimation Factor
settings.description: Multiplier for adjusting print time estimates. 100% shows original estimate. Higher values indicate longer actual print times.

settings.label: Nozzle ID
settings.description: The nozzle ID for an extruder train, such as "AA 0.4" and "BB 0.8".

settings.label: Nozzle Diameter
settings.description: The inner diameter of the nozzle. Change this setting when using a non-standard nozzle size.

settings.label: Offset with Extruder
settings.description: Apply the extruder offset to the coordinate system. Affects all extruders.

settings.label: Start GCode must be first
settings.description: This setting controls if the start-gcode is forced to always be the first g-code. Without this option other g-code, such as a T0 can be inserted before the start g-code.

settings.label: Extruder Prime Z Position
settings.description: The Z coordinate of the position where the nozzle primes at the start of printing.

settings.label: Absolute Extruder Prime Position
settings.description: Make the extruder prime position absolute rather than relative to the last-known location of the head.

settings.label: Maximum Speed X
settings.description: The maximum speed for the motor of the X-direction.

settings.label: Maximum Speed Y
settings.description: The maximum speed for the motor of the Y-direction.

settings.label: Maximum Speed Z
settings.description: The maximum speed for the motor of the Z-direction.

settings.label: Maximum Speed E
settings.description: The maximum speed of the filament.

settings.label: Maximum Acceleration X
settings.description: Maximum acceleration for the motor of the X-direction

settings.label: Maximum Acceleration Y
settings.description: Maximum acceleration for the motor of the Y-direction.

settings.label: Maximum Acceleration Z
settings.description: Maximum acceleration for the motor of the Z-direction.

settings.label: Maximum Filament Acceleration
settings.description: Maximum acceleration for the motor of the filament.

settings.label: Default Acceleration
settings.description: The default acceleration of print head movement.

settings.label: Default X-Y Jerk
settings.description: Default jerk for movement in the horizontal plane.

settings.label: Default Z Jerk
settings.description: Default jerk for the motor of the Z-direction.

settings.label: Default Filament Jerk
settings.description: Default jerk for the motor of the filament.

settings.label: Steps per Millimeter (X)
settings.description: How many steps of the stepper motor will result in one millimeter of movement in the X direction.

settings.label: Steps per Millimeter (Y)
settings.description: How many steps of the stepper motor will result in one millimeter of movement in the Y direction.

settings.label: Steps per Millimeter (Z)
settings.description: How many steps of the stepper motor will result in one millimeter of movement in the Z direction.

settings.label: Steps per Millimeter (E)
settings.description: How many steps of the stepper motors will result in moving the feeder wheel by one millimeter around its circumference.

settings.label: X Endstop in Positive Direction
settings.description: Whether the endstop of the X axis is in the positive direction (high X coordinate) or negative (low X coordinate).

settings.label: Y Endstop in Positive Direction
settings.description: Whether the endstop of the Y axis is in the positive direction (high Y coordinate) or negative (low Y coordinate).

settings.label: Z Endstop in Positive Direction
settings.description: Whether the endstop of the Z axis is in the positive direction (high Z coordinate) or negative (low Z coordinate).

settings.label: Minimum Feedrate
settings.description: The minimal movement speed of the print head.

settings.label: Feeder Wheel Diameter
settings.description: The diameter of the wheel that drives the material in the feeder.

settings.label: Scale Fan Speed To 0-1
settings.description: Scale the fan speed to be between 0 and 1 instead of between 0 and 256.

settings.label: Reset flow duration
settings.description: For any travel move longer than this value, the material flow is reset to the paths target flow

settings.label: Layer Height
settings.description: The height of each layer in mm. Higher values produce faster prints in lower resolution, lower values produce slower prints in higher resolution.

settings.label: Initial Layer Height
settings.description: The height of the initial layer in mm. A thicker initial layer makes adhesion to the build plate easier.

settings.label: Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single line. Generally, the width of each line should correspond to the width of the nozzle. However, slightly reducing this value could produce better prints.

settings.label: Wall Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single wall line.

settings.label: Outer Wall Line Width
settings.description: Width of the outermost wall line. By lowering this value, higher levels of detail can be printed.

settings.label: Inner Wall(s) Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single wall line for all wall lines except the outermost one.

settings.label: Top/Bottom Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single top/bottom line.

settings.label: Infill Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single infill line.

settings.label: Skirt/Brim Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single skirt or brim line.

settings.label: Support Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single support structure line.

settings.label: Support Interface Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single line of support roof or floor.

settings.label: Support Roof Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single support roof line.

settings.label: Support Floor Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single support floor line.

settings.label: Prime Tower Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single prime tower line.

settings.label: Initial Layer Line Width
settings.description: Multiplier of the line width on the first layer. Increasing this could improve bed adhesion.

settings.label: Wall Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train used for printing the walls. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Outer Wall Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train used for printing the outer wall. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Inner Wall Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train used for printing the inner walls. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Wall Thickness
settings.description: The thickness of the walls in the horizontal direction. This value divided by the wall line width defines the number of walls.

settings.label: Wall Line Count
settings.description: The number of walls. When calculated by the wall thickness, this value is rounded to a whole number.

settings.label: Wall Transition Length
settings.description: When transitioning between different numbers of walls as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the wall lines.

settings.label: Wall Distribution Count
settings.description: The number of walls, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer walls don't change in width.

settings.label: Wall Transitioning Threshold Angle
settings.description: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of walls. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no walls will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center walls, but may leave gaps or overextrude.

settings.label: Wall Transitioning Filter Distance
settings.description: If it would be transitioning back and forth between different numbers of walls in quick succession, don't transition at all. Remove transitions if they are closer together than this distance.

settings.label: Wall Transitioning Filter Margin
settings.description: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra wall and one less. This margin extends the range of line widths which follow to [Minimum Wall Line Width - Margin, 2 * Minimum Wall Line Width + Margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large line width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems.

settings.label: Outer Wall Wipe Distance
settings.description: Distance of a travel move inserted after the outer wall, to hide the Z seam better.

settings.label: Outer Wall Inset
settings.description: Inset applied to the path of the outer wall. If the outer wall is smaller than the nozzle, and printed after the inner walls, use this offset to get the hole in the nozzle to overlap with the inner walls instead of the outside of the model.

settings.label: Optimize Wall Printing Order
settings.description: Optimize the order in which walls are printed so as to reduce the number of retractions and the distance travelled. Most parts will benefit from this being enabled but some may actually take longer so please compare the print time estimates with and without optimization. First layer is not optimized when choosing brim as build plate adhesion type.

settings.label: Wall Ordering
settings.description: Determines the order in which walls are printed. Printing outer walls earlier helps with dimensional accuracy, as faults from inner walls cannot propagate to the outside. However printing them later allows them to stack better when overhangs are printed. When there is an uneven amount of total innner walls, the 'center last line' is always printed last.

settings.label: Alternate Extra Wall
settings.description: Prints an extra wall at every other layer. This way infill gets caught between these extra walls, resulting in stronger prints.

settings.label: Minimum Wall Line Width
settings.description: For thin structures around once or twice the nozzle size, the line widths need to be altered to adhere to the thickness of the model. This setting controls the minimum line width allowed for the walls. The minimum line widths inherently also determine the maximum line widths, since we transition from N to N+1 walls at some geometry thickness where the N walls are wide and the N+1 walls are narrow. The widest possible wall line is twice the Minimum Wall Line Width.

settings.label: Minimum Even Wall Line Width
settings.description: The minimum line width for normal polygonal walls. This setting determines at which model thickness we switch from printing a single thin wall line, to printing two wall lines. A higher Minimum Even Wall Line Width leads to a higher maximum odd wall line width. The maximum even wall line width is calculated as Outer Wall Line Width + 0.5 * Minimum Odd Wall Line Width.

settings.label: Minimum Odd Wall Line Width
settings.description: The minimum line width for middle line gap filler polyline walls. This setting determines at which model thickness we switch from printing two wall lines, to printing two outer walls and a single central wall in the middle. A higher Minimum Odd Wall Line Width leads to a higher maximum even wall line width. The maximum odd wall line width is calculated as 2 * Minimum Even Wall Line Width.

settings.label: Print Thin Walls
settings.description: Print pieces of the model which are horizontally thinner than the nozzle size.

settings.label: Minimum Feature Size
settings.description: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than the Minimum Feature Size will be widened to the Minimum Wall Line Width.

settings.label: Minimum Thin Wall Line Width
settings.description: Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum Feature Size) of the model. If the Minimum Wall Line Width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the wall will become as thick as the feature itself.

settings.label: Horizontal Expansion
settings.description: Amount of offset applied to all polygons in each layer. Positive values can compensate for too big holes; negative values can compensate for too small holes.

settings.label: Initial Layer Horizontal Expansion
settings.description: Amount of offset applied to all polygons in the first layer. A negative value can compensate for squishing of the first layer known as "elephant's foot".

settings.label: Hole Horizontal Expansion
settings.description: When greater than zero, the Hole Horizontal Expansion is the amount of offset applied to all holes in each layer. Positive values increase the size of the holes, negative values reduce the size of the holes. When this setting is enabled it can be further tuned with Hole Horizontal Expansion Max Diameter.

settings.label: Hole Horizontal Expansion Max Diameter
settings.description: When greater than zero, the Hole Horizontal Expansion is gradually applied on small holes (small holes are expanded more). When set to zero the Hole Horizontal Expansion will be applied to all holes. Holes larger than the Hole Horizontal Expansion Max Diameter are not expanded.

settings.label: Z Seam Alignment
settings.description: Starting point of each path in a layer. When paths in consecutive layers start at the same point a vertical seam may show on the print. When aligning these near a user specified location, the seam is easiest to remove. When placed randomly the inaccuracies at the paths' start will be less noticeable. When taking the shortest path the print will be quicker.

settings.label: Z Seam On Vertex
settings.description: Place the z-seam on a polygon vertex. Switching this off can place the seam between vertices as well. (Keep in mind that this won't override the restrictions on placing the seam on an unsupported overhang.)

settings.label: Z Seam Position
settings.description: The position near where to start printing each part in a layer. Note: For the 'Middle' option, the reference point differs critically based on Z Seam Relative setting - it will be the middle of the buildplate (absolute) or the middle of each object (relative), resulting in completely different seam placements.

settings.label: Z Seam X
settings.description: The X coordinate of the position near where to start printing each part in a layer. When Z Seam Relative is disabled, this is an absolute position on the buildplate. When enabled, this is relative to each object's center.

settings.label: Z Seam Y
settings.description: The Y coordinate of the position near where to start printing each part in a layer. When Z Seam Relative is disabled, this is an absolute position on the buildplate. When enabled, this is relative to each object's center.

settings.label: Seam Corner Preference
settings.description: Control how corners on the model outline influence the position of the seam. Hide Seam makes the seam more likely to occur on an inside corner. Expose Seam makes the seam more likely to occur on an outside corner. Hide or Expose Seam makes the seam more likely to occur at an inside or outside corner. Smart Hiding allows both inside and outside corners, but chooses inside corners more frequently, if appropriate.

settings.label: Z Seam Relative
settings.description: When enabled, the z seam coordinates are relative to each part's centre. When disabled, the coordinates define an absolute position on the build plate. This setting is critical for the 'Middle' Z Seam Position option: relative positioning places the seam at the middle of each object, while absolute positioning places it at the middle of the buildplate, resulting in completely different seam placements.

settings.label: Top Surface Skin Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train used for printing the top most skin. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Top Surface Skin Layers
settings.description: The number of top most skin layers. Usually only one top most layer is sufficient to generate higher quality top surfaces.

settings.label: Top Surface Skin Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single line of the areas at the top of the print.

settings.label: Top Surface Skin Pattern
settings.description: The pattern of the top most layers.

settings.label: Monotonic Top Surface Order
settings.description: Print top surface lines in an ordering that causes them to always overlap with adjacent lines in a single direction. This takes slightly more time to print, but makes flat surfaces look more consistent.

settings.label: Top Surface Skin Line Directions
settings.description: A list of integer line directions to use when the top surface skin layers use the lines or zig zag pattern. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the traditional default angles (45 and 135 degrees).

settings.label: Top Surface Expansion
settings.description: Determines how much the top surfaces are expanded beneath overlapping surfaces. By adjusting this value, you can ensure that the outer edges of the top surfaces are concealed by the layers above, resulting in a better visual quality, particularly for models with curved surfaces.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Skin Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train used for printing the bottom most skin. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Skin Layers
settings.description: The number of bottom most skin layers. Usually only one bottom most layer is sufficient to generate higher quality bottom surfaces.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Skin Line Width
settings.description: Width of a single line of the areas at the bottom of the print.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Skin Pattern
settings.description: The pattern of the bottom most layers.

settings.label: Monotonic Bottom Surface Order
settings.description: Print bottom surface lines in an ordering that causes them to always overlap with adjacent lines in a single direction. This takes slightly more time to print, but makes flat surfaces look more consistent.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Skin Line Directions
settings.description: A list of integer line directions to use when the bottom surface skin layers use the lines or zig zag pattern. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the traditional default angles (45 and 135 degrees).

settings.label: Top/Bottom Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train used for printing the top and bottom skin. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Top/Bottom Thickness
settings.description: The thickness of the top/bottom layers in the print. This value divided by the layer height defines the number of top/bottom layers.

settings.label: Top Thickness
settings.description: The thickness of the top layers in the print. This value divided by the layer height defines the number of top layers.

settings.label: Top Layers
settings.description: The number of top layers. When calculated by the top thickness, this value is rounded to a whole number.

settings.label: Bottom Thickness
settings.description: The thickness of the bottom layers in the print. This value divided by the layer height defines the number of bottom layers.

settings.label: Bottom Layers
settings.description: The number of bottom layers. When calculated by the bottom thickness, this value is rounded to a whole number.

settings.label: Initial Bottom Layers
settings.description: The number of initial bottom layers, from the build-plate upwards. When calculated by the bottom thickness, this value is rounded to a whole number.

settings.label: Top/Bottom Pattern
settings.description: The pattern of the top/bottom layers.

settings.label: Bottom Pattern Initial Layer
settings.description: The pattern on the bottom of the print on the first layer.

settings.label: Connect Top/Bottom Polygons
settings.description: Connect top/bottom skin paths where they run next to each other. For the concentric pattern enabling this setting greatly reduces the travel time, but because the connections can happen midway over infill this feature can reduce the top surface quality.

settings.label: Monotonic Top/Bottom Order
settings.description: Print top/bottom lines in an ordering that causes them to always overlap with adjacent lines in a single direction. This takes slightly more time to print, but makes flat surfaces look more consistent.

settings.label: Top/Bottom Line Directions
settings.description: A list of integer line directions to use when the top/bottom layers use the lines or zig zag pattern. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the traditional default angles (45 and 135 degrees).

settings.label: Small Top/Bottom Width
settings.description: Small top/bottom regions are filled with walls instead of the default top/bottom pattern. This helps to avoids jerky motions. Off for the topmost (air-exposed) layer by default (see 'Small Top/Bottom On Surface').

settings.label: Small Top/Bottom On Surface
settings.description: Enable small (up to 'Small Top/Bottom Width') regions on the topmost skinned layer (exposed to air) to be filled with walls instead of the default pattern.

settings.label: No Skin in Z Gaps
settings.description: When the model has small vertical gaps of only a few layers, there should normally be skin around those layers in the narrow space. Enable this setting to not generate skin if the vertical gap is very small. This improves printing time and slicing time, but technically leaves infill exposed to the air.

settings.label: Extra Skin Wall Count
settings.description: Replaces the outermost part of the top/bottom pattern with a number of concentric lines. Using one or two lines improves roofs that start on infill material.

settings.label: Enable Ironing
settings.description: Go over the top surface one additional time, but this time extruding very little material. This is meant to melt the plastic on top further, creating a smoother surface. The pressure in the nozzle chamber is kept high so that the creases in the surface are filled with material.

settings.label: Iron Only Highest Layer
settings.description: Only perform ironing on the very last layer of the mesh. This saves time if the lower layers don't need a smooth surface finish.

settings.label: Ironing Pattern
settings.description: The pattern to use for ironing top surfaces.

settings.label: Monotonic Ironing Order
settings.description: Print ironing lines in an ordering that causes them to always overlap with adjacent lines in a single direction. This takes slightly more time to print, but makes flat surfaces look more consistent.

settings.label: Ironing Line Spacing
settings.description: The distance between the lines of ironing.

settings.label: Ironing Flow
settings.description: The amount of material, relative to a normal skin line, to extrude during ironing. Keeping the nozzle filled helps filling some of the crevices of the top surface, but too much results in overextrusion and blips on the side of the surface.

settings.label: Ironing Inset
settings.description: A distance to keep from the edges of the model. Ironing all the way to the edge of the mesh may result in a jagged edge on your print.

settings.label: Ironing Speed
settings.description: The speed at which to pass over the top surface.

settings.label: Ironing Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which ironing is performed.

settings.label: Ironing Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change while performing ironing.

settings.label: Skin Overlap Percentage
settings.description: Adjust the amount of overlap between the walls and (the endpoints of) the skin-centerlines, as a percentage of the line widths of the skin lines and the innermost wall. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the skin. Note that, given an equal skin and wall line-width, any percentage over 50% may already cause any skin to go past the wall, because at that point the position of the nozzle of the skin-extruder may already reach past the middle of the wall.

settings.label: Skin Overlap
settings.description: Adjust the amount of overlap between the walls and (the endpoints of) the skin-centerlines. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the skin. Note that, given an equal skin and wall line-width, any value over half the width of the wall may already cause any skin to go past the wall, because at that point the position of the nozzle of the skin-extruder may already reach past the middle of the wall.

settings.label: Skin Removal Width
settings.description: The largest width of skin areas which are to be removed. Every skin area smaller than this value will disappear. This can help in limiting the amount of time and material spent on printing top/bottom skin at slanted surfaces in the model.

settings.label: Top Skin Removal Width
settings.description: The largest width of top skin areas which are to be removed. Every skin area smaller than this value will disappear. This can help in limiting the amount of time and material spent on printing top skin at slanted surfaces in the model.

settings.label: Bottom Skin Removal Width
settings.description: The largest width of bottom skin areas which are to be removed. Every skin area smaller than this value will disappear. This can help in limiting the amount of time and material spent on printing bottom skin at slanted surfaces in the model.

settings.label: Skin Expand Distance
settings.description: The distance the skins are expanded into the infill. Higher values makes the skin attach better to the infill pattern and makes the walls on neighboring layers adhere better to the skin. Lower values save amount of material used.

settings.label: Top Skin Expand Distance
settings.description: The distance the top skins are expanded into the infill. Higher values makes the skin attach better to the infill pattern and makes the walls on the layer above adhere better to the skin. Lower values save amount of material used.

settings.label: Bottom Skin Expand Distance
settings.description: The distance the bottom skins are expanded into the infill. Higher values makes the skin attach better to the infill pattern and makes the skin adhere better to the walls on the layer below. Lower values save amount of material used.

settings.label: Maximum Skin Angle for Expansion
settings.description: Top and/or bottom surfaces of your object with an angle larger than this setting, won't have their top/bottom skin expanded. This avoids expanding the narrow skin areas that are created when the model surface has a near vertical slope. An angle of 0° is horizontal and will cause no skin to be expanded, while an angle of 90° is vertical and will cause all skin to be expanded.

settings.label: Minimum Skin Width for Expansion
settings.description: Skin areas narrower than this are not expanded. This avoids expanding the narrow skin areas that are created when the model surface has a slope close to the vertical.

settings.label: Infill Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train used for printing infill. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Infill Density
settings.description: Adjusts the density of infill of the print.

settings.label: Infill Line Distance
settings.description: Distance between the printed infill lines. This setting is calculated by the infill density and the infill line width.

settings.label: Infill Pattern
settings.description:
The pattern of the infill material of the print.
  • The Line and Zig Zag infill swap direction on alternate layers, reducing material cost.
  • The Grid, Triangle, Tri-Hexagon, Cubic, Octet, Quarter Cubic, Cross, and Concentric patterns are fully printed every layer.
  • Gyroid, Honeycomb, Octagon, Cubic, Quarter Cubic, and Octet infill change with every layer to provide a more equal distribution of strength over each direction.
  • Lightning infill tries to minimize the infill, by only supporting the ceiling of the object.
⚠ Grid, Triangles, and Cubic infill patterns contain intersecting lines, that may cause your nozzle to bump into printed lines, and your printer to vibrate. Use with caution.

settings.label: Connect Infill Lines
settings.description: Connect the ends where the infill pattern meets the inner wall using a line which follows the shape of the inner wall. Enabling this setting can make the infill adhere to the walls better and reduce the effects of infill on the quality of vertical surfaces. Disabling this setting reduces the amount of material used.

settings.label: Connect Infill Polygons
settings.description: Connect infill paths where they run next to each other. For infill patterns which consist of several closed polygons, enabling this setting greatly reduces the travel time.

settings.label: Infill Line Directions
settings.description: A list of integer line directions to use. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the traditional default angles (45 and 135 degrees for the lines and zig zag patterns and 45 degrees for all other patterns).

settings.label: Infill X Offset
settings.description: The infill pattern is moved this distance along the X axis.

settings.label: Infill Y Offset
settings.description: The infill pattern is moved this distance along the Y axis.

settings.label: Randomize Infill Start
settings.description: Randomize which infill line is printed first. This prevents one segment becoming the strongest, but it does so at the cost of an additional travel move.

settings.label: Infill Line Multiplier
settings.description: Convert each infill line to this many lines. The extra lines do not cross over each other, but avoid each other. This makes the infill stiffer, but increases print time and material usage.

settings.label: Extra Infill Wall Count
settings.description:
Add extra walls around the infill area. Such walls can make top/bottom skin lines sag down less which means you need less top/bottom skin layers for the same quality at the cost of some extra material.
This feature can combine with the Connect Infill Polygons to connect all the infill into a single extrusion path without the need for travels or retractions if configured right.

settings.label: Cubic Subdivision Shell
settings.description: An addition to the radius from the center of each cube to check for the boundary of the model, as to decide whether this cube should be subdivided. Larger values lead to a thicker shell of small cubes near the boundary of the model.

settings.label: Infill Overlap Percentage
settings.description: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls as a percentage of the infill line width. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

settings.label: Infill Overlap
settings.description: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

settings.label: Infill Wipe Distance
settings.description: Distance of a travel move inserted after every infill line, to make the infill stick to the walls better. This option is similar to infill overlap, but without extrusion and only on one end of the infill line.

settings.label: Infill Layer Thickness
settings.description: The thickness per layer of infill material. This value should always be a multiple of the layer height and is otherwise rounded.

settings.label: Gradual Infill Steps
settings.description: Number of times to reduce the infill density by half when getting further below top surfaces. Areas which are closer to top surfaces get a higher density, up to the Infill Density.

settings.label: Gradual Infill Step Height
settings.description: The height of infill of a given density before switching to half the density.

settings.label: Infill Before Walls
settings.description: Print the infill before printing the walls. Printing the walls first may lead to more accurate walls, but overhangs print worse. Printing the infill first leads to sturdier walls, but the infill pattern might sometimes show through the surface.

settings.label: Minimum Infill Area
settings.description: Don't generate areas of infill smaller than this (use skin instead).

settings.label: Infill Support
settings.description: Print infill structures only where tops of the model should be supported. Enabling this reduces print time and material usage, but leads to ununiform object strength.

settings.label: Infill Overhang Angle
settings.description: The minimum angle of internal overhangs for which infill is added. At a value of 0° objects are totally filled with infill, 90° will not provide any infill.

settings.label: Infill Skin Support
settings.description: Print a solid infill pattern just below skin to avoid printing the skin over air.

settings.label: Skin Support Speed
settings.description: The speed at which skin support regions are printed.

settings.label: Skin Support Flow
settings.description: When printing skin support regions, the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

settings.label: Skin Support Density
settings.description: The density of the skin support layer. Values less than 100 will increase the gaps between the lines.

settings.label: Skin Support Fan Speed
settings.description: Percentage fan speed to use when printing skin support.

settings.label: Interlace Skin Support Lines
settings.description: When enabled, skin support lines will be printed interlaced, i.e. in 2 monotonic passes so that adjacent lines won't be printed just after each other. The lines of the first pass then have more time to cool down and are stronger when the second pass is added.

settings.label: Lightning Infill Support Angle
settings.description: Determines when a lightning infill layer has to support anything above it. Measured in the angle given the thickness of a layer.

settings.label: Lightning Infill Overhang Angle
settings.description: Determines when a lightning infill layer has to support the model above it. Measured in the angle given the thickness.

settings.label: Lightning Infill Prune Angle
settings.description: The endpoints of infill lines are shortened to save on material. This setting is the angle of overhang of the endpoints of these lines.

settings.label: Lightning Infill Straightening Angle
settings.description: The infill lines are straightened out to save on printing time. This is the maximum angle of overhang allowed across the length of the infill line.

settings.label: Infill Start/End Move Inwards Length
settings.description: When starting or ending infill print, add an inwards extrusion move so that the tips of the infill won't impact the outer wall. This can be useful when the infill is printed at very high speed.

settings.label: Infill Start Move Inwards Length
settings.description: When starting infill print, add an inwards extrusion move so that the tips of the infill won't impact the outer wall. This can be useful when the infill is printed at very high speed.

settings.label: Infill End Move Inwards Length
settings.description: When starting or ending infill print, add an inwards extrusion move so that the tips of the infill won't impact the outer wall. This can be useful when the infill is printed at very high speed.

settings.label: Default Printing Temperature
settings.description: The default temperature used for printing. This should be the "base" temperature of a material. All other print temperatures should use offsets based on this value

settings.label: Build Volume Temperature
settings.description: The temperature of the environment to print in. If this is 0, the build volume temperature will not be adjusted.

settings.label: Printing Temperature
settings.description: The temperature used for printing.

settings.label: Printing Temperature Initial Layer
settings.description: The temperature used for printing the first layer.

settings.label: Initial Printing Temperature
settings.description: The minimal temperature while heating up to the Printing Temperature at which printing can already start.

settings.label: Final Printing Temperature
settings.description: The temperature to which to already start cooling down just before the end of printing.

settings.label: Extrusion Cool Down Speed Modifier
settings.description: The extra speed by which the nozzle cools while extruding. The same value is used to signify the heat up speed lost when heating up while extruding.

settings.label: Default Build Plate Temperature
settings.description: The default temperature used for the heated build plate. This should be the "base" temperature of a build plate. All other print temperatures should use offsets based on this value

settings.label: Build Plate Temperature
settings.description: The temperature used for the heated build plate. If this is 0, the build plate is left unheated.

settings.label: Build Plate Temperature Initial Layer
settings.description: The temperature used for the heated build plate at the first layer. If this is 0, the build plate is left unheated during the first layer.

settings.label: Adhesion Tendency
settings.description: Surface adhesion tendency.

settings.label: Surface Energy
settings.description: Surface energy.

settings.label: Scaling Factor Shrinkage Compensation
settings.description: To compensate for the shrinkage of the material as it cools down, the model will be scaled with this factor.

settings.label: Horizontal Scaling Factor Shrinkage Compensation
settings.description: To compensate for the shrinkage of the material as it cools down, the model will be scaled with this factor in the XY-direction (horizontally).

settings.label: Vertical Scaling Factor Shrinkage Compensation
settings.description: To compensate for the shrinkage of the material as it cools down, the model will be scaled with this factor in the Z-direction (vertically).

settings.label: Crystalline Material
settings.description: Is this material the type that breaks off cleanly when heated (crystalline), or is it the type that produces long intertwined polymer chains (non-crystalline)?

settings.label: Anti-ooze Retracted Position
settings.description: How far the material needs to be retracted before it stops oozing.

settings.label: Anti-ooze Retraction Speed
settings.description: How fast the material needs to be retracted during a filament switch to prevent oozing.

settings.label: Break Preparation Retracted Position
settings.description: How far the filament can be stretched before it breaks, while heated.

settings.label: Break Preparation Retraction Speed
settings.description: How fast the filament needs to be retracted just before breaking it off in a retraction.

settings.label: Break Preparation Temperature
settings.description: The temperature used to purge material, should be roughly equal to the highest possible printing temperature.

settings.label: Break Retracted Position
settings.description: How far to retract the filament in order to break it cleanly.

settings.label: Break Retraction Speed
settings.description: The speed at which to retract the filament in order to break it cleanly.

settings.label: Break Temperature
settings.description: The temperature at which the filament is broken for a clean break.

settings.label: Flush Purge Speed
settings.description: How fast to prime the material after switching to a different material.

settings.label: Flush Purge Length
settings.description: How much material to use to purge the previous material out of the nozzle (in length of filament) when switching to a different material.

settings.label: End of Filament Purge Speed
settings.description: How fast to prime the material after replacing an empty spool with a fresh spool of the same material.

settings.label: End of Filament Purge Length
settings.description: How much material to use to purge the previous material out of the nozzle (in length of filament) when replacing an empty spool with a fresh spool of the same material.

settings.label: Maximum Park Duration
settings.description: How long the material can be kept out of dry storage safely.

settings.label: No Load Move Factor
settings.description: A factor indicating how much the filament gets compressed between the feeder and the nozzle chamber, used to determine how far to move the material for a filament switch.

settings.label: Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation: the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

settings.label: Wall Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on wall lines.

settings.label: Outer Wall Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on the outermost wall line.

settings.label: Inner Wall(s) Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on wall lines for all wall lines except the outermost one.

settings.label: Top Surface Outer Wall Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on the top surface outermost wall line.

settings.label: Top Surface Inner Wall(s) Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on top surface wall lines for all wall lines except the outermost one.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Outer Wall Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on the bottom surface outermost wall line.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Inner Wall(s) Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on bottom surface wall lines for all wall lines except the outermost one.

settings.label: Top/Bottom Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on top/bottom lines.

settings.label: Top Surface Skin Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on lines of the areas at the top of the print.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Skin Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on lines of the areas at the bottom of the print.

settings.label: Infill Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on infill lines.

settings.label: Skirt/Brim Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on skirt or brim lines.

settings.label: Support Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on support structure lines.

settings.label: Support Interface Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on lines of support roof or floor.

settings.label: Support Roof Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on support roof lines.

settings.label: Support Floor Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on support floor lines.

settings.label: Prime Tower Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on prime tower lines.

settings.label: Initial Layer Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation for the first layer: the amount of material extruded on the initial layer is multiplied by this value.

settings.label: Initial Layer Inner Wall Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on wall lines for all wall lines except the outermost one, but only for the first layer

settings.label: Initial Layer Outer Wall Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on the outermost wall line of the first layer.

settings.label: Initial Layer Bottom Flow
settings.description: Flow compensation on bottom lines of the first layer

settings.label: Standby Temperature
settings.description: The temperature of the nozzle when another nozzle is currently used for printing.

settings.label: Is support material
settings.description: Is this material typically used as a support material during printing.

settings.label: Gradual flow enabled
settings.description: Enable gradual flow changes. When enabled, the flow is gradually increased/decreased to the target flow. This is useful for printers with a bowden tube where the flow is not immediately changed when the extruder motor starts/stops.

settings.label: Gradual flow max acceleration
settings.description: Maximum acceleration for gradual flow changes

settings.label: Initial layer max flow acceleration
settings.description: Minimum speed for gradual flow changes for the first layer

settings.label: Gradual flow discretisation step size
settings.description: Duration of each step in the gradual flow change

settings.label: Pressure advance factor
settings.description: Tuning factor for pressure advance, which is meant to synchronize extrusion with motion

settings.label: Material Maximum Flow Rate
settings.description: Maximum flow rate that the printer can extrude for the material

settings.label: Print Speed
settings.description: The speed at which printing happens.

settings.label: Infill Speed
settings.description: The speed at which infill is printed.

settings.label: Wall Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the walls are printed.

settings.label: Outer Wall Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the outermost walls are printed. Printing the outer wall at a lower speed improves the final skin quality. However, having a large difference between the inner wall speed and the outer wall speed will affect quality in a negative way.

settings.label: Inner Wall Speed
settings.description: The speed at which all inner walls are printed. Printing the inner wall faster than the outer wall will reduce printing time. It works well to set this in between the outer wall speed and the infill speed.

settings.label: Top Surface Outer Wall Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the top surface outermost wall is printed.

settings.label: Top Surface Inner Wall Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the top surface inner walls are printed.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Outer Wall Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the bottom surface outermost wall is printed.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Inner Wall Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the bottom surface inner walls are printed.

settings.label: Top Surface Skin Speed
settings.description: The speed at which top surface skin layers are printed.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Skin Speed
settings.description: The speed at which bottom surface skin layers are printed.

settings.label: Top/Bottom Speed
settings.description: The speed at which top/bottom layers are printed.

settings.label: Support Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the support structure is printed. Printing support at higher speeds can greatly reduce printing time. The surface quality of the support structure is not important since it is removed after printing.

settings.label: Support Infill Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the infill of support is printed. Printing the infill at lower speeds improves stability.

settings.label: Support Interface Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the roofs and floors of support are printed. Printing them at lower speeds can improve overhang quality.

settings.label: Support Roof Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the roofs of support are printed. Printing them at lower speeds can improve overhang quality.

settings.label: Support Floor Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the floor of support is printed. Printing it at lower speed can improve adhesion of support on top of your model.

settings.label: Prime Tower Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the prime tower is printed. Printing the prime tower slower can make it more stable when the adhesion between the different filaments is suboptimal.

settings.label: Travel Speed
settings.description: The speed at which travel moves are made.

settings.label: Initial Layer Speed
settings.description: The speed for the initial layer. A lower value is advised to improve adhesion to the build plate. Does not affect the build plate adhesion structures themselves, like brim and raft.

settings.label: Initial Layer Print Speed
settings.description: The speed of printing for the initial layer. A lower value is advised to improve adhesion to the build plate.

settings.label: Initial Layer Travel Speed
settings.description: The speed of travel moves in the initial layer. A lower value is advised to prevent pulling previously printed parts away from the build plate. The value of this setting can automatically be calculated from the ratio between the Travel Speed and the Print Speed.

settings.label: Skirt/Brim Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the skirt and brim are printed. Normally this is done at the initial layer speed, but sometimes you might want to print the skirt or brim at a different speed.

settings.label: Z Hop Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the vertical Z movement is made for Z Hops. This is typically lower than the print speed since the build plate or machine's gantry is harder to move.

settings.label: Number of Slower Layers
settings.description: The first few layers are printed slower than the rest of the model, to get better adhesion to the build plate and improve the overall success rate of prints. The speed is gradually increased over these layers.

settings.label: Flow Equalization Ratio
settings.description: Extrusion width based correction factor on the speed. At 0% the movement speed is kept constant at the Print Speed. At 100% the movement speed is adjusted so that the flow (in mm³/s) is kept constant, i.e. lines half the normal Line Width are printed twice as fast and lines twice as wide are printed half as fast. A value larger than 100% can help to compensate for the higher pressure required to extrude wide lines.

settings.label: Enable Acceleration Control
settings.description: Enables adjusting the print head acceleration. Increasing the accelerations can reduce printing time at the cost of print quality.

settings.label: Enable Travel Acceleration
settings.description: Use a separate acceleration rate for travel moves. If disabled, travel moves will use the acceleration value of the printed line at their destination.

settings.label: Print Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which printing happens.

settings.label: Infill Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which infill is printed.

settings.label: Wall Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the walls are printed.

settings.label: Outer Wall Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the outermost walls are printed.

settings.label: Inner Wall Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which all inner walls are printed.

settings.label: Top Surface Outer Wall Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the top surface outermost walls are printed.

settings.label: Top Surface Inner Wall Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the top surface inner walls are printed.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Outer Wall Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the bottom surface outermost walls are printed.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Inner Wall Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the bottom surface inner walls are printed.

settings.label: Top Surface Skin Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which top surface skin layers are printed.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Skin Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which bottom surface skin layers are printed.

settings.label: Top/Bottom Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which top/bottom layers are printed.

settings.label: Support Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the support structure is printed.

settings.label: Support Infill Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the infill of support is printed.

settings.label: Support Interface Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the roofs and floors of support are printed. Printing them at lower acceleration can improve overhang quality.

settings.label: Support Roof Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the roofs of support are printed. Printing them at lower acceleration can improve overhang quality.

settings.label: Support Floor Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the floors of support are printed. Printing them at lower acceleration can improve adhesion of support on top of your model.

settings.label: Prime Tower Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the prime tower is printed.

settings.label: Travel Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which travel moves are made.

settings.label: Initial Layer Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration for the initial layer.

settings.label: Initial Layer Print Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration during the printing of the initial layer.

settings.label: Initial Layer Travel Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration for travel moves in the initial layer.

settings.label: Skirt/Brim Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the skirt and brim are printed. Normally this is done with the initial layer acceleration, but sometimes you might want to print the skirt or brim at a different acceleration.

settings.label: Enable Jerk Control
settings.description: Enables adjusting the jerk of print head when the velocity in the X or Y axis changes. Increasing the jerk can reduce printing time at the cost of print quality.

settings.label: Enable Travel Jerk
settings.description: Use a separate jerk rate for travel moves. If disabled, travel moves will use the jerk value of the printed line at their destination.

settings.label: Print Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change of the print head.

settings.label: Infill Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which infill is printed.

settings.label: Wall Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the walls are printed.

settings.label: Outer Wall Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the outermost walls are printed.

settings.label: Inner Wall Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which all inner walls are printed.

settings.label: Top Surface Outer Wall Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the top surface outermost walls are printed.

settings.label: Top Surface Inner Wall Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the top surface inner walls are printed.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Outer Wall Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the bottom surface outermost walls are printed.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Inner Wall Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the bottom surface inner walls are printed.

settings.label: Top Surface Skin Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which top surface skin layers are printed.

settings.label: Bottom Surface Skin Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which bottom surface skin layers are printed.

settings.label: Top/Bottom Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which top/bottom layers are printed.

settings.label: Support Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the support structure is printed.

settings.label: Support Infill Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the infill of support is printed.

settings.label: Support Interface Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the roofs and floors of support are printed.

settings.label: Support Roof Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the roofs of support are printed.

settings.label: Support Floor Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the floors of support are printed.

settings.label: Prime Tower Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the prime tower is printed.

settings.label: Travel Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which travel moves are made.

settings.label: Initial Layer Jerk
settings.description: The print maximum instantaneous velocity change for the initial layer.

settings.label: Initial Layer Print Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change during the printing of the initial layer.

settings.label: Initial Layer Travel Jerk
settings.description: The acceleration for travel moves in the initial layer.

settings.label: Skirt/Brim Jerk
settings.description: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the skirt and brim are printed.

settings.label: Enable Retraction
settings.description: Retract the filament when the nozzle is moving over a non-printed area.

settings.label: Retract at Layer Change
settings.description: Retract the filament when the nozzle is moving to the next layer.

settings.label: Retraction Distance
settings.description: The length of material retracted during a retraction move.

settings.label: Retraction Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the filament is retracted and primed during a retraction move.

settings.label: Retraction Retract Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the filament is retracted during a retraction move.

settings.label: Retraction Prime Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the filament is primed during a retraction move.

settings.label: Retraction Extra Prime Amount
settings.description: Some material can ooze away during a travel move, which can be compensated for here.

settings.label: Retraction Minimum Travel
settings.description: The minimum distance of travel needed for a retraction to happen at all. This helps to get fewer retractions in a small area.

settings.label: Maximum Retraction Count
settings.description: This setting limits the number of retractions occurring within the minimum extrusion distance window. Further retractions within this window will be ignored. This avoids retracting repeatedly on the same piece of filament, as that can flatten the filament and cause grinding issues.

settings.label: Minimum Extrusion Distance Window
settings.description: The window in which the maximum retraction count is enforced. This value should be approximately the same as the retraction distance, so that effectively the number of times a retraction passes the same patch of material is limited.

settings.label: Combing Mode
settings.description: Combing keeps the nozzle within already printed areas when traveling. This results in slightly longer travel moves but reduces the need for retractions. If combing is off, the material will retract and the nozzle moves in a straight line to the next point. It is also possible to avoid combing over top/bottom skin areas or to only comb within the infill.

settings.label: Max Comb Distance With No Retract
settings.description: When greater than zero, combing travel moves that are longer than this distance will use retraction. If set to zero, there is no maximum and combing moves will not use retraction.

settings.label: Inside Travel Avoid Distance
settings.description: The distance between the nozzle and already printed outer walls when travelling inside a model.

settings.label: Retract Before Outer Wall
settings.description: Always retract when moving to start an outer wall.

settings.label: Avoid Printed Parts When Traveling
settings.description: The nozzle avoids already printed parts when traveling. This option is only available when combing is enabled.

settings.label: Avoid Supports When Traveling
settings.description: The nozzle avoids already printed supports when traveling. This option is only available when combing is enabled.

settings.label: Travel Avoid Distance
settings.description: The distance between the nozzle and already printed parts when avoiding during travel moves.

settings.label: Layer Start at Z Seam
settings.description: Start printing at the Z seam position.

settings.label: Layer Start X
settings.description: The X coordinate of the position near where to find the part to start printing each layer.

settings.label: Layer Start Y
settings.description: The Y coordinate of the position near where to find the part to start printing each layer.

settings.label: Z Hop When Retracted
settings.description: Whenever a retraction is done, the build plate is lowered to create clearance between the nozzle and the print. It prevents the nozzle from hitting the print during travel moves, reducing the chance to knock the print from the build plate.

settings.label: Z Hop Only Over Printed Parts
settings.description: Only perform a Z Hop when moving over printed parts which cannot be avoided by horizontal motion by Avoid Printed Parts when Traveling.

settings.label: Z Hop Height
settings.description: The height difference when performing a Z Hop.

settings.label: Z Hop After Extruder Switch
settings.description: After the machine switched from one extruder to the other, the build plate is lowered to create clearance between the nozzle and the print. This prevents the nozzle from leaving oozed material on the outside of a print.

settings.label: Z Hop After Extruder Switch Height
settings.description: The height difference when performing a Z Hop after extruder switch.

settings.label: Enable Print Cooling
settings.description: Enables the print cooling fans while printing. The fans improve print quality on layers with short layer times and bridging / overhangs.

settings.label: Build Volume Fan Speed at Height
settings.description: The height at which the fans spin on regular fan speed. At the layers below the fan speed gradually increases from Initial Fan Speed to Regular Fan Speed.

settings.label: Build Volume Fan Speed at Layer
settings.description: The layer at which the build-volume fans spin on full fan speed. This value is calculated and rounded to a whole number.

settings.label: Initial Layers Build Volume Fan Speed
settings.description: The fan speed (as a percentage) for the auxiliary or build-volume fan, that is set until the layer specified at 'Build Volume Fan Speed at Layer' is reached. After that, the speed is set by 'Build Volume Fan Speed' instead (so not this 'Initial Layers' one).

settings.label: Build Volume Fan Speed
settings.description: The fan speed (as a percentage) for the auxiliary or build-volume fan, that is set from the moment that the layer specified at 'Build Volume Fan Speed at Layer' is reached and onwards. Before that, the speed is set by 'Initial Layers Build Volume Fan Speed' instead.

settings.label: Fan Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the print cooling fans spin.

settings.label: Regular Fan Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the fans spin before hitting the threshold. When a layer prints faster than the threshold, the fan speed gradually inclines towards the maximum fan speed.

settings.label: Maximum Fan Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the fans spin on the minimum layer time. The fan speed gradually increases between the regular fan speed and maximum fan speed when the threshold is hit.

settings.label: Regular/Maximum Fan Speed Threshold
settings.description: The layer time which sets the threshold between regular fan speed and maximum fan speed. Layers that print slower than this time use regular fan speed. For faster layers the fan speed gradually increases towards the maximum fan speed.

settings.label: Initial Fan Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the fans spin at the start of the print. In subsequent layers the fan speed is gradually increased up to the layer corresponding to Regular Fan Speed at Height.

settings.label: Regular Fan Speed at Height
settings.description: The height at which the fans spin on regular fan speed. At the layers below the fan speed gradually increases from Initial Fan Speed to Regular Fan Speed.

settings.label: Regular Fan Speed at Layer
settings.description: The layer at which the fans spin on regular fan speed. If regular fan speed at height is set, this value is calculated and rounded to a whole number.

settings.label: Minimum Layer Time
settings.description: The minimum time spent in a layer. This forces the printer to slow down, to at least spend the time set here in one layer. This allows the printed material to cool down properly before printing the next layer. Layers may still take shorter than the minimal layer time if Lift Head is disabled and if the Minimum Speed would otherwise be violated.

settings.label: Minimum Speed
settings.description: The minimum print speed, despite slowing down due to the minimum layer time. When the printer would slow down too much, the pressure in the nozzle would be too low and result in bad print quality.

settings.label: Lift Head
settings.description: When the minimum speed is hit because of minimum layer time, lift the head away from the print and wait the extra time until the minimum layer time is reached.

settings.label: Small Layer Printing Temperature
settings.description: Gradually reduce to this temperature when printing at reduced speeds because of minimum layer time.

settings.label: Cooling during extruder switch
settings.description:
Whether to activate the cooling fans during a nozzle switch. This can help reducing oozing by cooling the nozzle faster:
  • Unchanged: keep the fans as they were previously
  • Only last extruder: turn on the fan of the last used extruder, but turn the others off (if any). This is useful if you have completely separate extruders.
  • All fans: turn on all fans during nozzle switch. This is useful if you have a single cooling fan, or multiple fans that stay close to each other.

settings.label: Generate Support
settings.description: Generate structures to support parts of the model which have overhangs. Without these structures, such parts would collapse during printing.

settings.label: Support Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the support. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Support Infill Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the infill of the support. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: First Layer Support Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the first layer of support infill. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Support Interface Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the roofs and floors of the support. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Support Roof Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the roofs of the support. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Support Floor Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the floors of the support. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Support Structure
settings.description: Chooses between the techniques available to generate support. "Normal" support creates a support structure directly below the overhanging parts and drops those areas straight down. "Tree" support creates branches towards the overhanging areas that support the model on the tips of those branches, and allows the branches to crawl around the model to support it from the build plate as much as possible.

settings.label: Maximum Branch Angle
settings.description: The maximum angle of the branches while they grow around the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle to be able to have more reach.

settings.label: Branch Diameter
settings.description: The diameter of the thinnest branches of tree support. Thicker branches are more sturdy. Branches towards the base will be thicker than this.

settings.label: Trunk Diameter
settings.description: The diameter of the widest branches of tree support. A thicker trunk is more sturdy; a thinner trunk takes up less space on the build plate.

settings.label: Branch Diameter Angle
settings.description: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the tree support.

settings.label: Support Z Seam Away from Model
settings.description: Manage the spatial relationship between the z seam of the support structure and the actual 3D model. This control is crucial as it allows users to ensure the seamless removal of support structures post-printing, without inflicting damage or leaving marks on the printed model.

settings.label: Min Z Seam Distance from Model
settings.description: The distance between the model and its support structure at the z-axis seam.

settings.label: Support Placement
settings.description: Adjusts the placement of the support structures. The placement can be set to touching build plate or everywhere. When set to everywhere the support structures will also be printed on the model.

settings.label: Preferred Branch Angle
settings.description: The preferred angle of the branches, when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for branches to merge faster.

settings.label: Diameter Increase To Model
settings.description: The most the diameter of a branch that has to connect to the model may increase by merging with branches that could reach the buildplate. Increasing this reduces print time, but increases the area of support that rests on model

settings.label: Minimum Height To Model
settings.description: How tall a branch has to be if it is placed on the model. Prevents small blobs of support. This setting is ignored when a branch is supporting a support roof.

settings.label: Initial Layer Diameter
settings.description: Diameter every branch tries to achieve when reaching the buildplate. Improves bed adhesion.

settings.label: Branch Density
settings.description: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs, but the supports are harder to remove. Use Support Roof for very high values or ensure support density is similarly high at the top.

settings.label: Tip Diameter
settings.description: The diameter of the top of the tip of the branches of tree support.

settings.label: Limit Branch Reach
settings.description: Limit how far each branch should travel from the point it supports. This can make the support more sturdy, but will increase the amount of branches (and because of that material usage/print time)

settings.label: Optimal Branch Range
settings.description: A recomendation to how far branches can move from the points they support. Branches can violate this value to reach their destination (buildplate or a flat part of the model). Lowering this value will make the support more sturdy, but increase the amount of branches (and because of that material usage/print time)

settings.label: Rest Preference
settings.description: The preferred placement of the support structures. If structures can't be placed at the preferred location, they will be place elsewhere, even if that means placing them on the model.

settings.label: Support Overhang Angle
settings.description: The minimum angle of overhangs for which support is added. At a value of 0° all overhangs are supported, 90° will not provide any support.

settings.label: Support Pattern
settings.description: The pattern of the support structures of the print. The different options available result in sturdy or easy to remove support.

settings.label: Support Wall Line Count
settings.description: The number of walls with which to surround support infill. Adding a wall can make support print more reliably and can support overhangs better, but increases print time and material used.
