settings.label: Support Interface Wall Line Count
settings.description: The number of walls with which to surround support interface. Adding a wall can make support print more reliably and can support overhangs better, but increases print time and material used.

settings.label: Support Roof Wall Line Count
settings.description: The number of walls with which to surround support interface roof. Adding a wall can make support print more reliably and can support overhangs better, but increases print time and material used.

settings.label: Support Bottom Wall Line Count
settings.description: The number of walls with which to surround support interface floor. Adding a wall can make support print more reliably and can support overhangs better, but increases print time and material used.

settings.label: Connect Support Lines
settings.description: Connect the ends of the support lines together. Enabling this setting can make your support more sturdy and reduce underextrusion, but it will cost more material.

settings.label: Connect Support ZigZags
settings.description: Connect the ZigZags. This will increase the strength of the zig zag support structure.

settings.label: Support Density
settings.description: Adjusts the density of the support structure. A higher value results in better overhangs, but the supports are harder to remove.

settings.label: Support Line Distance
settings.description: Distance between the printed support structure lines. This setting is calculated by the support density.

settings.label: Initial Layer Support Line Distance
settings.description: Distance between the printed initial layer support structure lines. This setting is calculated by the support density.

settings.label: Support Infill Density Multiplier Initial Layer
settings.description: Multiplier for the infill on the initial layers of the support. Increasing this may help for bed adhesion.

settings.label: Support Infill Line Directions
settings.description: A list of integer line directions to use. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the default angle 0 degrees.

settings.label: Enable Support Brim
settings.description: Generate a brim within the support infill regions of the first layer. This brim is printed underneath the support, not around it. Enabling this setting increases the adhesion of support to the build plate.

settings.label: Support Brim Width
settings.description: The width of the brim to print underneath the support. A larger brim enhances adhesion to the build plate, at the cost of some extra material.

settings.label: Support Brim Line Count
settings.description: The number of lines used for the support brim. More brim lines enhance adhesion to the build plate, at the cost of some extra material.

settings.label: Support Z Distance
settings.description: Distance from the top/bottom of the support structure to the print. This gap provides clearance to remove the supports after the model is printed. The topmost support layer below the model might be a fraction of regular layers.

settings.label: Support Top Distance
settings.description: Distance from the top of the support to the print.

settings.label: Support Bottom Distance
settings.description: Distance from the print to the bottom of the support. Note that this is rounded up to the next layer height.

settings.label: Support X/Y Distance
settings.description: Distance of the support structure from the print in the X/Y directions.

settings.label: Support Distance Priority
settings.description: Whether the Support X/Y Distance overrides the Support Z Distance or vice versa. When X/Y overrides Z the X/Y distance can push away the support from the model, influencing the actual Z distance to the overhang. We can disable this by not applying the X/Y distance around overhangs.

settings.label: Minimum Support X/Y Distance
settings.description: Distance of the support structure from the overhang in the X/Y directions.

settings.label: Support Stair Step Height
settings.description: The height of the steps of the stair-like bottom of support resting on the model. A low value makes the support harder to remove, but too high values can lead to unstable support structures. Set to zero to turn off the stair-like behaviour.

settings.label: Support Stair Step Maximum Width
settings.description: The maximum width of the steps of the stair-like bottom of support resting on the model. A low value makes the support harder to remove, but too high values can lead to unstable support structures.

settings.label: Support Stair Step Minimum Slope Angle
settings.description: The minimum slope of the area for stair-stepping to take effect. Low values should make support easier to remove on shallower slopes, but really low values may result in some very counter-intuitive results on other parts of the model.

settings.label: Support Join Distance
settings.description: The maximum distance between support structures in the X/Y directions. When separate structures are closer together than this value, the structures merge into one.

settings.label: Support Horizontal Expansion
settings.description: Amount of offset applied to all support polygons in each layer. Positive values can smooth out the support areas and result in more sturdy support.

settings.label: Support Infill Layer Thickness
settings.description: The thickness per layer of support infill material. This value should always be a multiple of the layer height and is otherwise rounded.

settings.label: Gradual Support Infill Steps
settings.description: Number of times to reduce the support infill density by half when getting further below top surfaces. Areas which are closer to top surfaces get a higher density, up to the Support Infill Density.
settings.max: (999999 if support_line_distance == 0 else (20 - math.log(support_line_distance) / math.log(2))) if support_structure != 'tree' else 0

settings.label: Gradual Support Infill Step Height
settings.description: The height of support infill of a given density before switching to half the density.

settings.label: Minimum Support Area
settings.description: Minimum area size for support polygons. Polygons which have an area smaller than this value will not be generated.

settings.label: Enable Support Interface
settings.description: Generate a dense interface between the model and the support. This will create a skin at the top of the support on which the model is printed and at the bottom of the support, where it rests on the model.

settings.label: Enable Support Roof
settings.description: Generate a dense slab of material between the top of support and the model. This will create a skin between the model and support.

settings.label: Enable Support Floor
settings.description: Generate a dense slab of material between the bottom of the support and the model. This will create a skin between the model and support.

settings.label: Support Interface Thickness
settings.description: The thickness of the interface of the support where it touches with the model on the bottom or the top.

settings.label: Support Roof Thickness
settings.description: The thickness of the support roofs. This controls the amount of dense layers at the top of the support on which the model rests.

settings.label: Support Floor Thickness
settings.description: The thickness of the support floors. This controls the number of dense layers that are printed on top of places of a model on which support rests.

settings.label: Support Interface Density
settings.description: Adjusts the density of the roofs and floors of the support structure. A higher value results in better overhangs, but the supports are harder to remove.

settings.label: Support Roof Density
settings.description: The density of the roofs of the support structure. A higher value results in better overhangs, but the supports are harder to remove.

settings.label: Support Roof Line Distance
settings.description: Distance between the printed support roof lines. This setting is calculated by the Support Roof Density, but can be adjusted separately.

settings.label: Support Floor Density
settings.description: The density of the floors of the support structure. A higher value results in better adhesion of the support on top of the model.

settings.label: Support Floor Line Distance
settings.description: Distance between the printed support floor lines. This setting is calculated by the Support Floor Density, but can be adjusted separately.

settings.label: Support Interface Pattern
settings.description: The pattern with which the interface of the support with the model is printed.

settings.label: Support Roof Pattern
settings.description: The pattern with which the roofs of the support are printed.

settings.label: Support Floor Pattern
settings.description: The pattern with which the floors of the support are printed.

settings.label: Minimum Support Interface Area
settings.description: Minimum area size for support interface polygons. Polygons which have an area smaller than this value will be printed as normal support.

settings.label: Minimum Support Roof Area
settings.description: Minimum area size for the roofs of the support. Polygons which have an area smaller than this value will be printed as normal support.

settings.label: Minimum Support Floor Area
settings.description: Minimum area size for the floors of the support. Polygons which have an area smaller than this value will be printed as normal support.

settings.label: Support Interface Horizontal Expansion
settings.description: Amount of offset applied to the support interface polygons.

settings.label: Support Roof Horizontal Expansion
settings.description: Amount of offset applied to the roofs of the support.

settings.label: Support Floor Horizontal Expansion
settings.description: Amount of offset applied to the floors of the support.

settings.label: Support Interface Priority
settings.description: How support interface and support will interact when they overlap. Currently only implemented for support roof.

settings.label: Support Interface Line Directions
settings.description: A list of integer line directions to use. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the default angles (alternates between 45 and 135 degrees if interfaces are quite thick or 90 degrees).

settings.label: Support Roof Line Directions
settings.description: A list of integer line directions to use. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the default angles (alternates between 45 and 135 degrees if interfaces are quite thick or 90 degrees).

settings.label: Support Floor Line Directions
settings.description: A list of integer line directions to use. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the default angles (alternates between 45 and 135 degrees if interfaces are quite thick or 90 degrees).

settings.label: Fan Speed Override
settings.description: When enabled, the print cooling fan speed is altered for the skin regions immediately above the support.

settings.label: Supported Skin Fan Speed
settings.description: Percentage fan speed to use when printing the skin regions immediately above the support. Using a high fan speed can make the support easier to remove.

settings.label: Use Towers
settings.description: Use specialized towers to support tiny overhang areas. These towers have a larger diameter than the region they support. Near the overhang the towers' diameter decreases, forming a roof.

settings.label: Tower Diameter
settings.description: The diameter of a special tower.

settings.label: Maximum Tower-Supported Diameter
settings.description: Maximum diameter in the X/Y directions of a small area which is to be supported by a specialized support tower.

settings.label: Tower Roof Angle
settings.description: The angle of a rooftop of a tower. A higher value results in pointed tower roofs, a lower value results in flattened tower roofs.

settings.label: Drop Down Support Mesh
settings.description: Make support everywhere below the support mesh, so that there's no overhang in the support mesh.

settings.label: Scene Has Support Meshes
settings.description: There are support meshes present in the scene. This setting is controlled by Cura.

settings.label: Enable Prime Blob
settings.description: Whether to prime the filament with a blob before printing. Turning this setting on will ensure that the extruder will have material ready at the nozzle before printing. Printing Brim or Skirt can act like priming too, in which case turning this setting off saves some time.

settings.label: Extruder Prime X Position
settings.description: The X coordinate of the position where the nozzle primes at the start of printing.

settings.label: Extruder Prime Y Position
settings.description: The Y coordinate of the position where the nozzle primes at the start of printing.

settings.label: Build Plate Adhesion Type
settings.description: Different options that help to improve both priming your extrusion and adhesion to the build plate. Brim adds a single layer flat area around the base of your model to prevent warping. Raft adds a thick grid with a roof below the model. Skirt is a line printed around the model, but not connected to the model.

settings.label: Build Plate Adhesion Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the skirt/brim/raft. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Skirt/Brim Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the skirt or brim. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Raft Base Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the first layer of the raft. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Raft Middle Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the middle layer of the raft. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Raft Top Extruder
settings.description: The extruder train to use for printing the top layer(s) of the raft. This is used in multi-extrusion.

settings.label: Skirt Line Count
settings.description: Multiple skirt lines help to prime your extrusion better for small models. Setting this to 0 will disable the skirt.

settings.label: Skirt Height
settings.description: Printing the innermost skirt line with multiple layers makes it easy to remove the skirt.

settings.label: Skirt Distance
settings.description:
The horizontal distance between the skirt and the first layer of the print.
This is the minimum distance. Multiple skirt lines will extend outwards from this distance.

settings.label: Skirt/Brim Minimum Length
settings.description: The minimum length of the skirt or brim. If this length is not reached by all skirt or brim lines together, more skirt or brim lines will be added until the minimum length is reached. Note: If the line count is set to 0 this is ignored.

settings.label: Brim Width
settings.description: The distance from the model to the outermost brim line. A larger brim enhances adhesion to the build plate, but also reduces the effective print area.

settings.label: Brim Line Count
settings.description: The number of lines used for a brim. More brim lines enhance adhesion to the build plate, but also reduces the effective print area.

settings.label: Brim Distance
settings.description: The horizontal distance between the first brim line and the outline of the first layer of the print. A small gap can make the brim easier to remove while still providing the thermal benefits.

settings.label: Brim Replaces Support
settings.description: Enforce brim to be printed around the model even if that space would otherwise be occupied by support. This replaces some regions of the first layer of support by brim regions.

settings.label: Brim Location
settings.description: Print a brim on the outside of the model, inside, or both. Depending on the model, this helps reducing the amount of brim you need to remove afterwards, while ensuring a proper bed adhesion.

settings.label: Brim Avoid Margin
settings.description: A brim around a model may touch an other model where you don't want it. This removes all brim within this distance from brimless models.

settings.label: Smart Brim
settings.description: Swap print order of the innermost and second innermost brim lines. This improves brim removal.

settings.label: Raft Extra Margin
settings.description: If the raft is enabled, this is the extra raft area around the model which is also given a raft. Increasing this margin will create a stronger raft while using more material and leaving less area for your print.

settings.label: Raft Base Extra Margin
settings.description: If the raft base is enabled, this is the extra raft area around the model which is also given a raft. Increasing this margin will create a stronger raft while using more material and leaving less area for your print.

settings.label: Raft Middle Extra Margin
settings.description: If the raft middle is enabled, this is the extra raft area around the model which is also given a raft. Increasing this margin will create a stronger raft while using more material and leaving less area for your print.

settings.label: Raft Top Extra Margin
settings.description: If the raft top is enabled, this is the extra raft area around the model which is also given a raft. Increasing this margin will create a stronger raft while using more material and leaving less area for your print.

settings.label: Remove Raft Inside Corners
settings.description: Remove inside corners from the raft, causing the raft to become convex.

settings.label: Remove Raft Base Inside Corners
settings.description: Remove inside corners from the raft base, causing the raft to become convex.

settings.label: Remove Raft Middle Inside Corners
settings.description: Remove inside corners from the raft middle part, causing the raft to become convex.

settings.label: Remove Raft Top Inside Corners
settings.description: Remove inside corners from the raft top part, causing the raft to become convex.

settings.label: Raft Smoothing
settings.description: This setting controls how much inner corners in the raft outline are rounded. Inward corners are rounded to a semi circle with a radius equal to the value given here. This setting also removes holes in the raft outline which are smaller than such a circle.

settings.label: Raft Base Smoothing
settings.description: This setting controls how much inner corners in the raft base outline are rounded. Inward corners are rounded to a semi circle with a radius equal to the value given here. This setting also removes holes in the raft outline which are smaller than such a circle.

settings.label: Raft Middle Smoothing
settings.description: This setting controls how much inner corners in the raft middle outline are rounded. Inward corners are rounded to a semi circle with a radius equal to the value given here. This setting also removes holes in the raft outline which are smaller than such a circle.

settings.label: Raft Top Smoothing
settings.description: This setting controls how much inner corners in the raft top outline are rounded. Inward corners are rounded to a semi circle with a radius equal to the value given here. This setting also removes holes in the raft outline which are smaller than such a circle.

settings.label: Raft Air Gap
settings.description: The gap between the final raft layer and the first layer of the model. Only the first layer is raised by this amount to lower the bonding between the raft layer and the model. Makes it easier to peel off the raft.

settings.label: Initial Layer Z Overlap
settings.description:
Make the first and second layer of the model overlap in the Z direction to compensate for the filament lost in the airgap. All models above the first model layer will be shifted down by this amount.
It may be noted that sometimes the second layer is printed below initial layer because of this setting. This is intended behavior

settings.label: Raft Base Thickness
settings.description: Layer thickness of the base raft layer. This should be a thick layer which sticks firmly to the printer build plate.

settings.label: Raft Base Line Width
settings.description: Width of the lines in the base raft layer. These should be thick lines to assist in build plate adhesion.

settings.label: Raft Base Line Spacing
settings.description: The distance between the raft lines for the base raft layer. Wide spacing makes for easy removal of the raft from the build plate.

settings.label: Raft Base Infill Overlap Percentage
settings.description: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft base, as a percentage of the infill line width. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

settings.label: Raft Base Infill Overlap
settings.description: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft base. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

settings.label: Raft Middle Layers
settings.description: The number of layers between the base and the surface of the raft. These comprise the main thickness of the raft. Increasing this creates a thicker, sturdier raft.

settings.label: Raft Middle Thickness
settings.description: Layer thickness of the middle raft layer.

settings.label: Raft Middle Line Width
settings.description: Width of the lines in the middle raft layer. Making the second layer extrude more causes the lines to stick to the build plate.

settings.label: Raft Middle Spacing
settings.description: The distance between the raft lines for the middle raft layer. The spacing of the middle should be quite wide, while being dense enough to support the top raft layers.

settings.label: Raft Interface Z Offset
settings.description: When printing the first layer of the raft interface, translate by this offset to customize the adhesion between base and interface. A negative offset should improve the adhesion.

settings.label: Raft Interface Infill Overlap Percentage
settings.description: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft interface, as a percentage of the infill line width. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

settings.label: Raft Interface Infill Overlap
settings.description: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft interface. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

settings.label: Raft Top Layers
settings.description: The number of top layers on top of the 2nd raft layer. These are fully filled layers that the model sits on. 2 layers result in a smoother top surface than 1.

settings.label: Raft Top Layer Thickness
settings.description: Layer thickness of the top raft layers.

settings.label: Raft Top Line Width
settings.description: Width of the lines in the top surface of the raft. These can be thin lines so that the top of the raft becomes smooth.

settings.label: Raft Top Spacing
settings.description: The distance between the raft lines for the top raft layers. The spacing should be equal to the line width, so that the surface is solid.

settings.label: Raft Surface Z Offset
settings.description: When printing the first layer of the raft surface, translate by this offset to customize the adhesion between interface and surface. A negative offset should improve the adhesion.

settings.label: Monotonic Raft Top Surface Order
settings.description: Print raft top surface lines in an ordering that causes them to always overlap with adjacent lines in a single direction. This takes slightly more time to print, but makes the surface look more consistent, which is also visible on the model bottom surface.

settings.label: Raft Surface Infill Overlap Percentage
settings.description: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft surface, as a percentage of the infill line width. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

settings.label: Raft Surface Infill Overlap
settings.description: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft surface. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

settings.label: Raft Wall Count
settings.description: The number of contours to print around the linear pattern of the raft.

settings.label: Raft Base Wall Count
settings.description: The number of contours to print around the linear pattern in the base layer of the raft.

settings.label: Raft Middle Wall Count
settings.description: The number of contours to print around the linear pattern in the middle layers of the raft.

settings.label: Raft Top Wall Count
settings.description: The number of contours to print around the linear pattern in the top layers of the raft.

settings.label: Raft Print Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the raft is printed.

settings.label: Raft Base Print Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the base raft layer is printed. This should be printed quite slowly, as the volume of material coming out of the nozzle is quite high.

settings.label: Raft Middle Print Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the middle raft layer is printed. This should be printed quite slowly, as the volume of material coming out of the nozzle is quite high.

settings.label: Raft Top Print Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the top raft layers are printed. These should be printed a bit slower, so that the nozzle can slowly smooth out adjacent surface lines.

settings.label: Raft Print Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the raft is printed.

settings.label: Raft Base Print Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the base raft layer is printed.

settings.label: Raft Middle Print Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the middle raft layer is printed.

settings.label: Raft Top Print Acceleration
settings.description: The acceleration with which the top raft layers are printed.

settings.label: Raft Print Jerk
settings.description: The jerk with which the raft is printed.

settings.label: Raft Base Print Jerk
settings.description: The jerk with which the base raft layer is printed.

settings.label: Raft Middle Print Jerk
settings.description: The jerk with which the middle raft layer is printed.

settings.label: Raft Top Print Jerk
settings.description: The jerk with which the top raft layers are printed.

settings.label: Raft Fan Speed
settings.description: The fan speed for the raft.

settings.label: Raft Base Fan Speed
settings.description: The fan speed for the base raft layer.

settings.label: Raft Middle Fan Speed
settings.description: The fan speed for the middle raft layer.

settings.label: Raft Top Fan Speed
settings.description: The fan speed for the top raft layers.

settings.label: Raft Flow
settings.description: The amount of material, relative to a normal extrusion line, to extrude during raft printing. Having an increased flow may improve adhesion and raft structural strength.

settings.label: Raft Base Flow
settings.description: The amount of material, relative to a normal extrusion line, to extrude during raft base printing. Having an increased flow may improve adhesion and raft structural strength.

settings.label: Raft Interface Flow
settings.description: The amount of material, relative to a normal extrusion line, to extrude during raft interface printing. Having an increased flow may improve adhesion and raft structural strength.

settings.label: Raft Surface Flow
settings.description: The amount of material, relative to a normal extrusion line, to extrude during raft surface printing. Having an increased flow may improve adhesion and raft structural strength.

settings.label: Scan the first layer
settings.description: Whether to scan the first layer for layer adhesion problems.

settings.label: Enable Prime Tower
settings.description: Print a tower next to the print which serves to prime the material after each nozzle switch.

settings.label: Prime Tower Type
settings.description:
How to generate the prime tower:
  • Normal: create a bucket in which secondary materials are primed
  • Interleaved: create a prime tower as sparse as possible. This will save time and filament, but is only possible if the used materials adhere to each other

settings.label: Prime Tower Size
settings.description: The width of the prime tower.

settings.label: Prime Tower Minimum Volume
settings.description: The minimum volume for each layer of the prime tower in order to purge enough material.

settings.label: Prime Tower Maximum Bridging Distance
settings.description: The maximum length of the branches which may be printed over the air.

settings.label: Prime Tower Minimum Shell Thickness
settings.description: The minimum thickness of the prime tower shell. You may increase it to make the prime tower stronger.

settings.label: Prime Tower X Position
settings.description: The x coordinate of the position of the prime tower.
settings.min: resolveOrValue('prime_tower_size') + (resolveOrValue('prime_tower_base_size') if (resolveOrValue('adhesion_type') == 'raft' or resolveOrValue('prime_tower_brim_enable')) else 0) - (machine_width / 2 if machine_center_is_zero else 0)
settings.max: (machine_width / 2 if machine_center_is_zero else machine_width) - (resolveOrValue('prime_tower_base_size') if (resolveOrValue('adhesion_type') == 'raft' or resolveOrValue('prime_tower_brim_enable')) else 0)

settings.label: Prime Tower Y Position
settings.description: The y coordinate of the position of the prime tower.
settings.min: (machine_depth / -2 if machine_center_is_zero else 0) + (resolveOrValue('prime_tower_base_size') if (resolveOrValue('adhesion_type') == 'raft' or resolveOrValue('prime_tower_brim_enable')) else 0)
settings.max: (machine_depth / 2 - resolveOrValue('prime_tower_size') if machine_center_is_zero else machine_depth - resolveOrValue('prime_tower_size')) - (resolveOrValue('prime_tower_base_size') if (resolveOrValue('adhesion_type') == 'raft' or resolveOrValue('prime_tower_brim_enable')) else 0)

settings.label: Wipe Inactive Nozzle on Prime Tower
settings.description: After printing the prime tower with one nozzle, wipe the oozed material from the other nozzle off on the prime tower.

settings.label: Prime Tower Base
settings.description: By enabling this setting, your prime-tower will get a brim, even if the model doesn't. If you want a sturdier base for a high tower, you can increase the base height.

settings.label: Prime Tower Base Size
settings.description: The width of the prime tower brim/base. A larger base enhances adhesion to the build plate, but also reduces the effective print area.

settings.label: Prime Tower Base Height
settings.description: The height of the prime tower base. Increasing this value will result in a more sturdy prime tower because the base will be wider. If this setting is too low, the prime tower will not have a sturdy base.

settings.label: Prime Tower Base Slope
settings.description: The magnitude factor used for the slope of the prime tower base. If you increase this value, the base will become slimmer. If you decrease it, the base will become thicker.

settings.label: Prime Tower Raft Line Spacing
settings.description: The distance between the raft lines for the unique prime tower raft layer. Wide spacing makes for easy removal of the raft from the build plate.

settings.label: Enable Ooze Shield
settings.description: Enable exterior ooze shield. This will create a shell around the model which is likely to wipe a second nozzle if it's at the same height as the first nozzle.

settings.label: Ooze Shield Angle
settings.description: The maximum angle a part in the ooze shield will have. With 0 degrees being vertical, and 90 degrees being horizontal. A smaller angle leads to less failed ooze shields, but more material.

settings.label: Ooze Shield Distance
settings.description: Distance of the ooze shield from the print, in the X/Y directions.

settings.label: Nozzle Switch Retraction Distance
settings.description: The amount of retraction when switching extruders. Set to 0 for no retraction at all. This should generally be the same as the length of the heat zone.

settings.label: Nozzle Switch Retraction Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the filament is retracted. A higher retraction speed works better, but a very high retraction speed can lead to filament grinding.

settings.label: Nozzle Switch Retract Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the filament is retracted during a nozzle switch retract.

settings.label: Nozzle Switch Prime Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the filament is pushed back after a nozzle switch retraction.

settings.label: Nozzle Switch Extra Prime Amount
settings.description: Extra material to prime after nozzle switching.

settings.label: Generate Interlocking Structure
settings.description: At the locations where models touch, generate an interlocking beam structure. This improves the adhesion between models, especially models printed in different materials.

settings.label: Interlocking Beam Width
settings.description: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

settings.label: Interlocking Structure Orientation
settings.description: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

settings.label: Interlocking Beam Layer Count
settings.description: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

settings.label: Interlocking Depth
settings.description: The distance from the boundary between models to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

settings.label: Interlocking Boundary Avoidance
settings.description: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

settings.label: Multi-material Precision
settings.description: The precision of the details when generating multi-material shapes based on painting data. A lower precision will provide more details, but increase the slicing time and memory.

settings.label: Multi-material Depth
settings.description: The depth of the painted details inside the model. A higher depth will provide a better interlocking, but increase slicing time and memory. Set a very high value to go as deep as possible. The actually calculated depth may vary.

settings.label: Union Overlapping Volumes
settings.description: Ignore the internal geometry arising from overlapping volumes within a mesh and print the volumes as one. This may cause unintended internal cavities to disappear.

settings.label: Remove All Holes
settings.description: Remove the holes in each layer and keep only the outside shape. This will ignore any invisible internal geometry. However, it also ignores layer holes which can be viewed from above or below.

settings.label: Extensive Stitching
settings.description: Extensive stitching tries to stitch up open holes in the mesh by closing the hole with touching polygons. This option can introduce a lot of processing time.

settings.label: Keep Disconnected Faces
settings.description: Normally Cura tries to stitch up small holes in the mesh and remove parts of a layer with big holes. Enabling this option keeps those parts which cannot be stitched. This option should be used as a last resort option when everything else fails to produce proper g-code.

settings.label: Merged Meshes Overlap
settings.description: Make meshes which are touching each other overlap a bit. This makes them bond together better.

settings.label: Remove Mesh Intersection
settings.description: Remove areas where multiple meshes are overlapping with each other. This may be used if merged dual material objects overlap with each other.

settings.label: Alternate Mesh Removal
settings.description: Switch to which mesh intersecting volumes will belong with every layer, so that the overlapping meshes become interwoven. Turning this setting off will cause one of the meshes to obtain all of the volume in the overlap, while it is removed from the other meshes.

settings.label: Remove Empty First Layers
settings.description: Remove empty layers beneath the first printed layer if they are present. Disabling this setting can cause empty first layers if the Slicing Tolerance setting is set to Exclusive or Middle.

settings.label: Maximum Resolution
settings.description: The minimum size of a line segment after slicing. If you increase this, the mesh will have a lower resolution. This may allow the printer to keep up with the speed it has to process g-code and will increase slice speed by removing details of the mesh that it can't process anyway.

settings.label: Maximum Travel Resolution
settings.description: The minimum size of a travel line segment after slicing. If you increase this, the travel moves will have less smooth corners. This may allow the printer to keep up with the speed it has to process g-code, but it may cause model avoidance to become less accurate.

settings.label: Maximum Deviation
settings.description: The maximum deviation allowed when reducing the resolution for the Maximum Resolution setting. If you increase this, the print will be less accurate, but the g-code will be smaller. Maximum Deviation is a limit for Maximum Resolution, so if the two conflict the Maximum Deviation will always be held true.

settings.label: Maximum Extrusion Area Deviation
settings.description: The maximum extrusion area deviation allowed when removing intermediate points from a straight line. An intermediate point may serve as width-changing point in a long straight line. Therefore, if it is removed, it will cause the line to have a uniform width and, as a result, lose (or gain) a bit of extrusion area. If you increase this you may notice slight under- (or over-) extrusion in between straight parallel walls, as more intermediate width-changing points will be allowed to be removed. Your print will be less accurate, but the g-code will be smaller.

settings.label: Enable Fluid Motion
settings.description: When enabled tool paths are corrected for printers with smooth motion planners. Small movements that deviate from the general tool path direction are smoothed to improve fluid motions.

settings.label: Fluid Motion Shift Distance
settings.description: Distance points are shifted to smooth the path

settings.label: Fluid Motion Small Distance
settings.description: Distance points are shifted to smooth the path

settings.label: Fluid Motion Angle
settings.description: If a toolpath-segment deviates more than this angle from the general motion it is smoothed.

settings.label: Print Sequence
settings.description: Whether to print all models one layer at a time or to wait for one model to finish, before moving on to the next. One at a time mode is possible if a) only one extruder is enabled and b) all models are separated in such a way that the whole print head can move in between and all models are lower than the distance between the nozzle and the X/Y axes.

settings.label: Set Print Sequence Manually
settings.description: Allows you to order the object list to manually set the print sequence. First object from the list will be printed first.

settings.label: Infill Mesh
settings.description: Use this mesh to modify the infill of other meshes with which it overlaps. Replaces infill regions of other meshes with regions for this mesh. It's suggested to only print one Wall and no Top/Bottom Skin for this mesh.

settings.label: Mesh Processing Rank
settings.description: Determines the priority of this mesh when considering multiple overlapping infill meshes. Areas where multiple infill meshes overlap will take on the settings of the mesh with the highest rank. An infill mesh with a higher rank will modify the infill of infill meshes with lower rank and normal meshes.

settings.label: Cutting Mesh
settings.description: Limit the volume of this mesh to within other meshes. You can use this to make certain areas of one mesh print with different settings and with a whole different extruder.

settings.label: Mold
settings.description: Print models as a mold, which can be cast in order to get a model which resembles the models on the build plate.

settings.label: Minimal Mold Width
settings.description: The minimal distance between the outside of the mold and the outside of the model.

settings.label: Mold Roof Height
settings.description: The height above horizontal parts in your model which to print mold.

settings.label: Mold Angle
settings.description: The angle of overhang of the outer walls created for the mold. 0° will make the outer shell of the mold vertical, while 90° will make the outside of the model follow the contour of the model.

settings.label: Support Mesh
settings.description: Use this mesh to specify support areas. This can be used to generate support structure.

settings.label: Anti Overhang Mesh
settings.description: Use this mesh to specify where no part of the model should be detected as overhang. This can be used to remove unwanted support structure.

settings.label: Surface Mode
settings.description: Treat the model as a surface only, a volume, or volumes with loose surfaces. The normal print mode only prints enclosed volumes. "Surface" prints a single wall tracing the mesh surface with no infill and no top/bottom skin. "Both" prints enclosed volumes like normal and any remaining polygons as surfaces.

settings.label: Spiralize Outer Contour
settings.description: Spiralize smooths out the Z move of the outer edge. This will create a steady Z increase over the whole print. This feature turns a solid model into a single walled print with a solid bottom. This feature should only be enabled when each layer only contains a single part.

settings.label: Smooth Spiralized Contours
settings.description: Smooth the spiralized contours to reduce the visibility of the Z seam (the Z seam should be barely visible on the print but will still be visible in the layer view). Note that smoothing will tend to blur fine surface details.

settings.label: Relative Extrusion
settings.description: Use relative extrusion rather than absolute extrusion. Using relative E-steps makes for easier post-processing of the g-code. However, it's not supported by all printers and it may produce very slight deviations in the amount of deposited material compared to absolute E-steps. Irrespective of this setting, the extrusion mode will always be set to absolute before any g-code script is output.

settings.label: Slicing Tolerance
settings.description: Vertical tolerance in the sliced layers. The contours of a layer are normally generated by taking cross sections through the middle of each layer's thickness (Middle). Alternatively each layer can have the areas which fall inside of the volume throughout the entire thickness of the layer (Exclusive) or a layer has the areas which fall inside anywhere within the layer (Inclusive). Inclusive retains the most details, Exclusive makes for the best fit and Middle stays closest to the original surface.

settings.label: Infill Travel Optimization
settings.description: When enabled, the order in which the infill lines are printed is optimized to reduce the distance travelled. The reduction in travel time achieved very much depends on the model being sliced, infill pattern, density, etc. Note that, for some models that have many small areas of infill, the time to slice the model may be greatly increased.

settings.label: Flow Temperature Graph
settings.description: Data linking material flow (in mm3 per second) to temperature (degrees Celsius).

settings.label: Minimum Polygon Circumference
settings.description: Polygons in sliced layers that have a circumference smaller than this amount will be filtered out. Lower values lead to higher resolution mesh at the cost of slicing time. It is meant mostly for high resolution SLA printers and very tiny 3D models with a lot of details.

settings.label: Break Up Support In Chunks
settings.description: Skip some support line connections to make the support structure easier to break away. This setting is applicable to the Zig Zag support infill pattern.

settings.label: Support Chunk Size
settings.description: Leave out a connection between support lines once every N millimeter to make the support structure easier to break away.

settings.label: Support Chunk Line Count
settings.description: Skip one in every N connection lines to make the support structure easier to break away.

settings.label: Enable Draft Shield
settings.description: This will create a wall around the model, which traps (hot) air and shields against exterior airflow. Especially useful for materials which warp easily.

settings.label: Draft Shield X/Y Distance
settings.description: Distance of the draft shield from the print, in the X/Y directions.

settings.label: Draft Shield Limitation
settings.description: Set the height of the draft shield. Choose to print the draft shield at the full height of the model or at a limited height.

settings.label: Draft Shield Height
settings.description: Height limitation of the draft shield. Above this height no draft shield will be printed.

settings.label: Make Overhang Printable
settings.description: Change the geometry of the printed model such that minimal support is required. Steep overhangs will become shallow overhangs. Overhanging areas will drop down to become more vertical.

settings.label: Maximum Model Angle
settings.description: The maximum angle of overhangs after the they have been made printable. At a value of 0° all overhangs are replaced by a piece of model connected to the build plate, 90° will not change the model in any way.

settings.label: Maximum Overhang Hole Area
settings.description: The maximum area of a hole in the base of the model before it's removed by Make Overhang Printable.  Holes smaller than this will be retained.  A value of 0 mm² will fill all holes in the models base.

settings.label: Enable Coasting
settings.description: Coasting replaces the last part of an extrusion path with a travel path. The oozed material is used to print the last piece of the extrusion path in order to reduce stringing.

settings.label: Coasting Volume
settings.description: The volume otherwise oozed. This value should generally be close to the nozzle diameter cubed.

settings.label: Minimum Volume Before Coasting
settings.description: The smallest volume an extrusion path should have before allowing coasting. For smaller extrusion paths, less pressure has been built up in the bowden tube and so the coasted volume is scaled linearly. This value should always be larger than the Coasting Volume.

settings.label: Coasting Speed
settings.description: The speed by which to move during coasting, relative to the speed of the extrusion path. A value slightly under 100% is advised, since during the coasting move the pressure in the bowden tube drops.

settings.label: Cross 3D Pocket Size
settings.description: The size of pockets at four-way crossings in the cross 3D pattern at heights where the pattern is touching itself.

settings.label: Cross Infill Density Image
settings.description: The file location of an image of which the brightness values determine the minimal density at the corresponding location in the infill of the print.

settings.label: Cross Fill Density Image for Support
settings.description: The file location of an image of which the brightness values determine the minimal density at the corresponding location in the support.

settings.label: Enable Conical Support
settings.description: Make support areas smaller at the bottom than at the overhang.

settings.label: Conical Support Angle
settings.description: The angle of the tilt of conical support. With 0 degrees being vertical, and 90 degrees being horizontal. Smaller angles cause the support to be more sturdy, but consist of more material. Negative angles cause the base of the support to be wider than the top.

settings.label: Conical Support Minimum Width
settings.description: Minimum width to which the base of the conical support area is reduced. Small widths can lead to unstable support structures.

settings.label: Fuzzy Skin
settings.description: Randomly jitter while printing the outer wall, so that the surface has a rough and fuzzy look.

settings.label: Fuzzy Skin Outside Only
settings.description: Jitter only the parts' outlines and not the parts' holes.

settings.label: Fuzzy Skin Thickness
settings.description: The width within which to jitter. It's advised to keep this below the outer wall width, since the inner walls are unaltered.

settings.label: Fuzzy Skin Density
settings.description: The average density of points introduced on each polygon in a layer. Note that the original points of the polygon are discarded, so a low density results in a reduction of the resolution.

settings.label: Fuzzy Skin Point Distance
settings.description: The average distance between the random points introduced on each line segment. Note that the original points of the polygon are discarded, so a high smoothness results in a reduction of the resolution. This value must be higher than half the Fuzzy Skin Thickness.

settings.label: Flow Rate Compensation Max Extrusion Offset
settings.description: The maximum distance in mm to move the filament to compensate for changes in flow rate.

settings.label: Flow Rate Compensation Factor
settings.description: How far to move the filament in order to compensate for changes in flow rate, as a percentage of how far the filament would move in one second of extrusion.

settings.label: Use Adaptive Layers
settings.description: Adaptive layers computes the layer heights depending on the shape of the model.

settings.label: Adaptive Layers Maximum Variation
settings.description: The maximum allowed height different from the base layer height.

settings.label: Adaptive Layers Variation Step Size
settings.description: The difference in height of the next layer height compared to the previous one.

settings.label: Adaptive Layers Topography Size
settings.description: Target horizontal distance between two adjacent layers. Reducing this setting causes thinner layers to be used to bring the edges of the layers closer together.

settings.label: Overhanging Wall Angle
settings.description: Walls that overhang more than this angle will be printed using overhanging wall settings. When the value is 90, no walls will be treated as overhanging. Overhang that gets supported by support will not be treated as overhang either. Furthermore, any line that's less than half overhanging will also not be treated as overhang.

settings.label: Minimum Layer Time with Overhang
settings.description: The minimum time spent in a layer that contains overhanging extrusions. This forces the printer to slow down, to at least spend the time set here in one layer. This allows the printed material to cool down properly before printing the next layer. Layers may still take shorter than the minimal layer time if Lift Head is disabled and if the Minimum Speed would otherwise be violated.

settings.label: Minimum Overhang Segment Length
settings.description: When trying to apply the minimum layer time specific for overhanging layers, it will be applied only if at least one consecutive overhanging extrusion move is longer than this value.

settings.label: Seam Overhanging Wall Angle
settings.description: Try to prevent seams on walls that overhang more than this angle. When the value is 90, no walls will be treated as overhanging.

settings.label: Overhanging Wall Speeds
settings.description: Overhanging walls will be printed at a percentage of their normal print speed. You can specify multiple values, so that even more overhanging walls will be printed even slower, e.g. by setting [75, 50, 25]

settings.label: Enable Bridge Settings
settings.description: Detect bridges and modify print speed, flow and fan settings while bridges are printed.

settings.label: Minimum Bridge Wall Length
settings.description: Unsupported walls shorter than this will be printed using the normal wall settings. Longer unsupported walls will be printed using the bridge wall settings.

settings.label: Bridge Skin Support Threshold
settings.description: If a skin region is supported for less than this percentage of its area, print it using the bridge settings. Otherwise it is printed using the normal skin settings.

settings.label: Bridge Wall Coasting
settings.description: This controls the distance the extruder should coast immediately before a bridge wall begins. Coasting before the bridge starts can reduce the pressure in the nozzle and may produce a flatter bridge.

settings.label: Bridge Wall Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the bridge walls are printed.

settings.label: Bridge Wall Flow
settings.description: When printing bridge walls, the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

settings.label: Bridge Skin Speed
settings.description: The speed at which bridge skin regions are printed.

settings.label: Bridge Skin Flow
settings.description: When printing bridge skin regions, the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

settings.label: Bridge Skin Density
settings.description: The density of the bridge skin layer. Values less than 100 will increase the gaps between the skin lines.

settings.label: Bridge Fan Speed
settings.description: Percentage fan speed to use when printing bridge walls and skin.

settings.label: Interlace Bridge Lines
settings.description: When enabled, bridging lines will be printed interlaced, i.e. in 2 monotonic passes so that adjacent lines won't be printed just after each other. The lines of the first pass then have more time to cool down and are stronger when the second pass is added.

settings.label: Bridge Has Multiple Layers
settings.description: If enabled, the second and third layers above the air are printed using the following settings. Otherwise, those layers are printed using the normal settings.

settings.label: Bridge Second Skin Speed
settings.description: Print speed to use when printing the second bridge skin layer.

settings.label: Bridge Second Skin Flow
settings.description: When printing the second bridge skin layer, the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

settings.label: Bridge Second Skin Density
settings.description: The density of the second bridge skin layer. Values less than 100 will increase the gaps between the skin lines.

settings.label: Bridge Second Skin Fan Speed
settings.description: Percentage fan speed to use when printing the second bridge skin layer.

settings.label: Bridge Third Skin Speed
settings.description: Print speed to use when printing the third bridge skin layer.

settings.label: Bridge Third Skin Flow
settings.description: When printing the third bridge skin layer, the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

settings.label: Bridge Third Skin Density
settings.description: The density of the third bridge skin layer. Values less than 100 will increase the gaps between the skin lines.

settings.label: Bridge Third Skin Fan Speed
settings.description: Percentage fan speed to use when printing the third bridge skin layer.

settings.label: Wipe Nozzle Between Layers
settings.description: Whether to include nozzle wipe G-Code between layers (maximum 1 per layer). Enabling this setting could influence behavior of retract at layer change. Please use Wipe Retraction settings to control retraction at layers where the wipe script will be working.

settings.label: Material Volume Between Wipes
settings.description: Maximum material that can be extruded before another nozzle wipe is initiated. If this value is less than the volume of material required in a layer, the setting has no effect in this layer, i.e. it is limited to one wipe per layer.

settings.label: Wipe Retraction Enable
settings.description: Retract the filament when the nozzle is moving over a non-printed area.

settings.label: Wipe Retraction Distance
settings.description: Amount to retract the filament so it does not ooze during the wipe sequence.

settings.label: Wipe Retraction Extra Prime Amount
settings.description: Some material can ooze away during a wipe travel moves, which can be compensated for here.

settings.label: Wipe Retraction Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the filament is retracted and primed during a wipe retraction move.

settings.label: Wipe Retraction Retract Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the filament is retracted during a wipe retraction move.

settings.label: Wipe Retraction Prime Speed
settings.description: The speed at which the filament is primed during a wipe retraction move.

settings.label: Wipe Pause
settings.description: Pause after the unretract.

settings.label: Wipe Z Hop
settings.description: When wiping, the build plate is lowered to create clearance between the nozzle and the print. It prevents the nozzle from hitting the print during travel moves, reducing the chance to knock the print from the build plate.

settings.label: Wipe Z Hop Height
settings.description: The height difference when performing a Z Hop.

settings.label: Wipe Hop Speed
settings.description: Speed to move the z-axis during the hop.

settings.label: Wipe Brush X Position
settings.description: X location where wipe script will start.

settings.label: Wipe Repeat Count
settings.description: Number of times to move the nozzle across the brush.

settings.label: Wipe Move Distance
settings.description: The distance to move the head back and forth across the brush.

settings.label: Small Hole Max Size
settings.description: Holes and part outlines with a diameter smaller than this will be printed using Small Feature Speed.

settings.label: Small Feature Max Length
settings.description: Feature outlines that are shorter than this length will be printed using Small Feature Speed.

settings.label: Small Feature Speed
settings.description: Small features will be printed at this percentage of their normal print speed. Slower printing can help with adhesion and accuracy.

settings.label: Small Feature Initial Layer Speed
settings.description: Small features on the first layer will be printed at this percentage of their normal print speed. Slower printing can help with adhesion and accuracy.

settings.label: Alternate Wall Directions
settings.description: Alternate wall directions every other layer and inset. Useful for materials that can build up stress, like for metal printing.

settings.label: Group Outer Walls
settings.description: Outer walls of different islands in the same layer are printed in sequence. When enabled the amount of flow changes is limited because walls are printed one type at a time, when disabled the number of travels between islands is reduced because walls in the same islands are grouped.

settings.label: Retraction During Travel Move
settings.description:
The ratio of retraction performed during the travel move, with the remainder completed while the nozzle is stationary, before traveling
  • When 0, the entire retraction is performed while stationary, before the travel begins
  • When 100, the entire retraction is performed during the travel move, bypassing the stationary phase

settings.label: Keep Retracting During Travel
settings.description: When retraction during travel is enabled, and there is more than enough time to perform a full retract during a travel move, spread the retraction over the whole travel move with a lower retraction speed, so that we do not travel with a non-retracting nozzle. This can help reducing oozing.

settings.label: Prime During Travel Move
settings.description:
The ratio of priming performed during the travel move, with the remainder completed while the nozzle is stationary, after traveling
  • When 0, the entire priming is performed while stationary, after the travel ends
  • When 100, the entire priming is performed during the travel move, allowing the print to start immediately

settings.label: Scarf Seam Length
settings.description: Determines the length of the scarf seam, a seam type that should make the Z seam less visible. Must be higher than 0 to be effective.

settings.label: Scarf Seam Start Height
settings.description: The ratio of the selected layer height at which the scarf seam will begin. A lower number will result in a larger seam height. Must be lower than 100 to be effective.

settings.label: Scarf Seam Step Length
settings.description: Determines the length of each step in the flow change when extruding along the scarf seam. A smaller distance will result in a more precise but also more complex G-code.

settings.label: Outer Wall Start Speed Ratio
settings.description: This is the ratio of the top speed to start with when printing an outer wall.

settings.label: Outer Wall Start Acceleration
settings.description: This is the acceleration with which to reach the top speed when printing an outer wall.

settings.label: Outer Wall End Speed Ratio
settings.description: This is the ratio of the top speed to end with when printing an outer wall.

settings.label: Outer Wall End Deceleration
settings.description: This is the deceleration with which to end printing an outer wall.

settings.label: Outer Wall Speed Split Distance
settings.description: This is the maximum length of an extrusion path when splitting a longer path to apply the outer wall acceleration/deceleration. A smaller distance will create a more precise but also more verbose G-Code.

settings.label: Enable Print Process Reporting
settings.description: Enable print process reporting for setting threshold values for possible fault detection.

settings.label: Flow Warning
settings.description: Limit on the flow warning for detection.

settings.label: Flow Limit
settings.description: Limit on flow anomaly for detection.

settings.label: Print temperature Warning
settings.description: Limit on Print temperature warning for detection.

settings.label: Print temperature Limit
settings.description: Limit on Print Temperature anomaly for detection.

settings.label: Build Volume temperature Warning
settings.description: Limit on Build Volume Temperature warning for detection.

settings.label: Build Volume temperature Limit
settings.description: Limit on Build Volume temperature Anomaly for detection.

settings.label: Center Object
settings.description: Whether to center the object on the middle of the build platform (0,0), instead of using the coordinate system in which the object was saved.

settings.label: Mesh Position X
settings.description: Offset applied to the object in the x direction.

settings.label: Mesh Position Y
settings.description: Offset applied to the object in the y direction.

settings.label: Mesh Position Z
settings.description: Offset applied to the object in the z direction. With this you can perform what was used to be called 'Object Sink'.

settings.label: Mesh Rotation Matrix
settings.description: Transformation matrix to be applied to the model when loading it from file.
